newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African budget could cut STC, MST taxes.
newsitem.headline: S.African budget could cut STC, MST taxes.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel may opt to reduce or even scrap the Secondary Tax on Companies (STC) and the Marketable Securities Tax (MST), Old Mutual chief economist Dave Mohr said on Tuesday.
In a pre-budget briefing, Mohr said such a move would not have a significant impact on government revenues but would give a clear signal of an investor-friendly budget.
STC, levied on dividends, was cut to 12.5 percent from 25 percent in last year's budget while MST, levied on share transactions, was reduced at the same time to 0.5 percent from 1.0 percent.
Overall, however, there was little scope for significant tax changes in the 1997/98 budget which Manuel will present to parliament on Wednesday.
Mohr expected no increase in value added tax (VAT), although "sin" taxes on tobacco and alcohol were likely to be raised, along with the fuel levy.
On income tax, there would be some relief for fiscal drag and the government might also announce a dividend policy for public corporations, he said.
